title: i18n: the flow runner reads `translation.flows.FLOW.label` for its header and completion toast, falling back to the served `flowLabel` (stage 2 of objectstack-ai/objectstack#20318)
body:
This card carries the objectui half (stage 2) of objectstack-ai/objectstack#20318: the flow runner reads `translation.flows.FLOW.label`. objectstack-ai/objectstack#20318 keeps the served label (stage 1, objectstack-ai/objectstack#20633) and the ledger flip that follows this card's landing.

Filing gate: **④ a coordination node**, the per-layer child of an in-flight card. Filed by the `domain:spec` execution seat 2 (`session_014EJ1ED8X4MMrT18BhVx4tx`, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#18549) from the stage-1 ACCEPT on objectstack-ai/objectstack#20318. ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading belong to triage. ⛔ Not a claim.

## Why this is owed

objectstack triage graded objectstack-ai/objectstack#20318 **ENFORCE** by the maintainer's criterion: translating a flow's label is mainstream (the Salesforce Translation Workbench translates Flow labels). Today nothing in objectui reads `translation.flows.FLOW.label`, and no surface displays the flow's own label. The `domain:spec` seat 4 measured that on objectui `797a30f4` (objectstack-ai/objectstack#20318, comment `5880531686`):
- `FlowRunner.tsx` reads only `flows.FLOW.screens` (`localizeScreen`, about :219–:233).
- The runner `DialogTitle` (about :462) is the screen title or `flowRunner.title`.
- The completion toast (about :385) interpolates `flowName`, the API name.
- The launcher's notices use the action's label or `Flow "NAME"`.

## The served shape this reader consumes (objectstack-ai/objectstack#20633, at-tier PASS)

- `data.flowLabel` (optional string) is on every 200 from `POST /api/v1/automation/NAME/trigger` and `POST /api/v1/automation/NAME/runs/RUN_ID/resume`: paused, finished, refused or skipped.
- It is not on a 400 `FLOW_FAILED`, nor on the 404 / 409 / 422 refusals.
- It is the flow definition's authored label, verbatim. For a subflow chain it is the addressed parent's label, never the child's.
- `AutomationResult.flowLabel` in `@objectstack/spec` (`contracts/automation-service.ts`) declares it, and `TriggerFlowResponseSchema.data` mirrors it.

## What the reader does (the direction triage set; ⛔ not a ruling on UI design)

- `FlowRunner` keeps `flowLabel` from the trigger and resume responses (`ScreenFlowState` gains it). Two hosts mount `FlowRunner` (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` and `RecordDetailView.tsx`), so the read belongs in `FlowRunner`.
- The displayed label resolves as: the active locale's `translation.flows.FLOW.label`, then `flowLabel`, then `flowName`.
- It gets a display slot: the runner header, and the completion toast in place of the API name.
- Pins: a zh bundle and an en fallback, and a flow with no translation showing its authored label.

## Sequencing

- The reader reads an optional field, so it can be written against the declared shape now. It takes effect once the console serves a backend that includes objectstack-ai/objectstack#20633.
- After this lands and the objectstack console pin moves past it, objectstack-ai/objectstack#20318 flips its ledger row (`translation.json` `flows.children.label`), drops the container's `authorWarn`, and rewrites the `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx` bullet (the `domain:cli` seat's pointer `5863837992`).

Dedupe words: `flows label translation FlowRunner` · `flowLabel runner header` · `translation.flows label reader`
